```{r}
library(tidyverse)
spotify <- read_csv("https://proback.github.io/264_fall_2026/Data/spotify.csv")
```

## What is lubridate? {auto-animate="true"}

 - lubridate is a package that comes installed automatically with tidyverse
 - It is used to work with dates/times that may be otherwise difficult to format
 - It does this by turning poorly formatted and hard to work with dates into date-times
 
 

## Date-time Format {auto-animate="true"}

 - Date-times are the standard formats for dates and times
 - year-month-date hour:minute:second timezone
 - eg. 2026-10-28 09:30:00 UTC
 
## Extracting Dates & Date-times {auto-animate="true"}

```{.r code-line-numbers="1-3|4|5-6"}
mdy_hms("January 24th, 2017 at 5:00:00pm")
dmy_hms("22 Aug, 2019, 3:55:56 AM")
ymd("'99 3/12")
yq("2020 Q3")
parse_date_time("2020-1-25", "ymd")
parse_date_time("22:40:16", "HMS")
```

```{r}
mdy_hms("January 24th, 2017 at 5:00:00pm")
dmy_hms("22 Aug, 2019, 3:55:56 AM")
ymd("'99 3/12")
yq("2020 Q3")
parse_date_time("2020-1-25", "ymd")
parse_date_time("22:40:16", "HMS")
```

## Calculations using Date-times {auto-animate="true"}
``` {.r code-line-numbers="1-3|5-7"}
d1 = parse_date_time("2020-1-24", "ymd")
d2 = parse_date_time("2020-2-07", "ymd")
d2 - d1 # given in days

t1 = parse_date_time("09:30:00", "HMS")
t2 = parse_date_time("10:50:00", "HMS")
t2 - t1 # given in hours IF difference > 1 hr

```

```{r}
d1 = parse_date_time("2020-1-24", "ymd")
d2 = parse_date_time("2020-2-07", "ymd")
d2 - d1 # given in days

t1 = parse_date_time("09:30:00", "HMS")
t2 = parse_date_time("10:50:00", "HMS")
t2 - t1 # given in hours IF difference > 1 hr
```



## More functions of lubridate {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
td <- today(tzone = "")
td

as.character(wday(td, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE))

am(now(tzone = ""))
```

## More functions of lubridate: Intervals {auto-animate="true"}
```{r}
#| echo: true

interval <- interval(ymd("1969-01-01"), ymd("1989-01-01"))

ymd("1979-01-01") %within% interval
ymd("2001-01-01") %within% interval
```

## How can we use lubridate (pt 1)? {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
lunchtime <- tibble(
  name = c("Jim", "Sharon", "Beth", "Charles", "Jim II: The Sequel", "Mary"),
  clocked_out = c("12:01:01", "13:33:47", "12:02:45", "11:27:09", "12:22:22", "11:10:20"),
  clocked_in = c("12:45:00", "14:03:47", "14:50:23", "11:56:58", "12:45:00", "11:16:45")
)
lunchtime
```

## How can we use lubridate (pt 1)? {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
lunchtime |>
  mutate(clocked_out = parse_date_time(clocked_out, "HMS"),
         clocked_in = parse_date_time(clocked_in, "HMS")) |>
  mutate(hour_out = hour(clocked_out)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour_out)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Hour Clocked Out by # of Employees",
       x = "Hour Clocked Out",
       y = "# of Employees")
```

## How can we use lubridate (pt 1)? {auto-animate="true"}

```{r}
#| echo: true
lunchtime |>
  mutate(clocked_out = parse_date_time(clocked_out, "HMS"),
         clocked_in = parse_date_time(clocked_in, "HMS")) |>
  mutate(break_time = clocked_in - clocked_out) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = name, fill = name, y = break_time)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(title = "Break Time by Employee",
       x = "",
       y = "Break Time",
       fill = "Employee") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

## How can we use lubridate (pt 1)? {auto-animate="true"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
lunchtime |>
  mutate(clocked_out = parse_date_time(clocked_out, "HMS"),
         clocked_in = parse_date_time(clocked_in, "HMS"),
         break_time = as.double(clocked_in - clocked_out),
         mins_early = 30 - break_time) |>
  select(name, break_time, mins_early)
  
```

## How can we use lubridate (pt 2)? {auto-animate="true"}
```{r}
birthdays <- tibble(
  name = c("Jim", "Sharon", "Beth", "Charles", "Jim II: The Sequel", "Mary"),
  birthday = c("2005-01-24 23:39:37", "2004-04-03 12:34:23", "1999-09-19 2:06:00", "1984-03-01 19:56:12", "2014-06-09 14:22:20", "1966-12-08 09:22:23")
)
birthdays
```


## How can we use lubridate (pt 2)? {auto-animate="true"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
birthdays |>
  mutate(birthday = ymd_hms(birthday),
         morning_birthday = am(birthday),
         weekday = wday(birthday, label = TRUE)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = weekday, fill = morning_birthday)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Weekday of Birth and Morning Birthday",
    x = "Weekday",
    y = "# of People",
    fill = "Born in the Morning"
  )
```
## How can we use lubridate (pt 2)? {auto-animate="true"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
gen_x <- interval(ymd("1965-01-01"), ymd("1980-12-31"))
millennial <- interval(ymd("1981-01-01"), ymd("1996-12-31"))
gen_z <- interval(ymd("1997-01-01"), ymd("2012-01-01"))
gen_alpha <- interval(ymd("2013-01-01"), ymd("2025-12-31"))
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
birthdays |>
  mutate(birthday = ymd_hms(birthday),
         gen = case_when(
           birthday %within% gen_alpha  ~ "Gen Alpha",
           birthday %within% gen_z      ~ "Gen Z",
           birthday %within% millennial ~ "Millennial",
           birthday %within% gen_x      ~ "Gen X",
           .default = "Other"),
         gen = factor(gen, levels = c("Gen X", "Millennial", "Gen Z", "Gen Alpha", "Other")))
```
